key_insight: Odd elastic moduli persist at high symmetry in strain-gradient continua, but non-Hermitian elastodynamics requires anisotropy.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports designing active, nonreciprocal metamaterials whose anisotropy enables elastic-wave amplification and attenuation.
method: Classify fourth-, fifth-, and sixth-order odd stiffness tensors across 3D point-group symmetries.
Derive governing equations, higher-order boundary conditions, and the generalized acoustic tensor using dynamic virtual work.
Numerically analyze wave dispersion in a transversely hemitropic continuum.
evidence_signal: Numerical analysis of a transversely hemitropic continuum demonstrates exceptional points and simultaneous amplification and attenuation of elastic-wave components, while isotropic and hemitropic acoustic tensors remain Hermitian.
watch_item: The abstract reports theoretical and numerical results; experimental validation and microstructure-to-continuum homogenization remain future steps.
paper_title: Odd Elasticity in Strain-Gradient Continua: Anisotropy Classification and Non-Hermitian Elastodynamics
